newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to appeal WTO Sports Illustrated verdict.
newsitem.headline: Canada to appeal WTO Sports Illustrated verdict.

text.p: Canada plans to appeal a decision by a World Trade Organization (WTO) dispute panel against its protectionist policies against foreign magazines like Sports Illustrated, officials said on Friday.
Trade Minister Art Eggleton scheduled an afternoon news conference today to signal Canada's intentions, which Canadian Heritage Minister Sheila Copps said on Thursday would be to appeal.
The panel ruled in favor of the United States, which had charged that Canada was violating WTO rules by taxing Canadian editions of U.S. magazines -- so-called split-run editions.

The 1995 Canadian law targeted Time Warner Inc's Sports Illustrated in particular by referring to split runs that started after March 26, 1993, just days before Sports Illustrated Canada first came out.

The law slapped an 80 percent excise tax on advertising in split runs distributed in Canada containing any Canadian-oriented ads and more than 20 percent editorial material designed for another market.
Canada will have 60 days to appeal. The appeal panel is to give its verdict 60 to 90 days from the date of the appeal.
